newsitem.title: GERMANY: GLOBAL COFFEE CONSUMPTION SET FOR RISE - ROTHFOS.
newsitem.headline: GLOBAL COFFEE CONSUMPTION SET FOR RISE - ROTHFOS.

text.p: Global coffee consumption in 1997/98 is forecast at 101 million bags, rounded, compared with 99.6 million in 1996/97, German trader Bernhard Rothfos GmbH said in its quarterly digest.
The 1997/98 figure was made up of 76.0 million bags forecast to be consumed in importing countries and just under 25 million bags likely to be consumed in producer countries.

The 1996/97 figure consisted of a 24.1 million bag estimate of consumption in producing countries, which was unchanged from a May estimate although prices in producer countries had risen, and a 75.5 million bag estimate for importing countries' use.
The latter figure was up from an estimated 75 million bag consumption figure envisaged for 1996/97 in May and compared with an identical 75 million figure given for in 1995/96.

The exportable crop in 1997/98 was pegged at 75.06 million bags, little changed from 75.21 million bags in 1996/97, which Rothfos said "indicates the delicate balance which continues to exist between production and disappearance levels."
